Port Coquitlam condos for sale: apartment-style homes in strata buildings. The Greater Vancouver REALTORS® benchmark for apartments (condos) in Port Coquitlam was $551,200 in October 2026 (-7.6% over a year). Before you offer, read the strata documents: the depreciation report, meeting minutes, bylaws and fees.
Port Coquitlam condos sold, November 2025 to October 2026

202 condos sold in Port Coquitlam with a median price of $557,500 (the middle half sold between $465,625 and $628,375), taking a median of 28 days to sell at 97.6% of the last list price; 5% sold above list. They had a median $614 per square foot, a median year built of 2008 and a median strata fee of $431 a month.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Condos: streets and boundaries

items.t: The second condo cluster is the Lougheed Highway frontage at Shaughnessy Square, 2099 Lougheed Highway, where residential strata sits in the same address as retail strata units.
Downtown is bounded in practice by the Coquitlam River to the west and the Mary Hill slope to the east, with Gates Park at 2300 Reeve Street at the downtown shelf's north end.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Condos: the housing stock

items.t: Mayfair Terrace, 2266 Atkins Avenue, is the city's one verified age-restricted strata: freehold strata plan LMS4171, built 2000, 4 storeys, 46 units, with a published 55-plus position and a mandatory service plan on top of strata fees.
Shaughnessy Square, 2099 Lougheed Highway, was built in 2002 per the building directory, which records pets allowed with restrictions for the residential strata.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Condos: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Apartment zoning downtown is RA1 and RA2 under Zoning Bylaw, 2008, No. 3630: RA1 allows a floor area ratio (FAR) of 1.0, rising with structured parking and amenity contributions, and RA2 allows FAR up to 2.5, concentrated downtown and along main roads. - Zoning Bylaw 2008.pdf

Every new downtown condo building needs a development permit: the City designates multi-family residential development as a Development Permit Area in the Official Community Plan (OCP) for form and character, under OCP Bylaw, 2013, No. 3838.
A 55-plus bylaw is the only age bylaw a strata may enforce, under sections 123.1 and 123.2 of the Strata Property Act — the frame for Mayfair Terrace's registered position at 2266 Atkins Avenue.
At Mayfair Terrace, ask for the service agreement with the Form B: the mandatory base service plan sits on top of strata fees, so the strata fee alone understates the monthly cost.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Condos: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The building beside the newest strata is rental, not strata: Kew Lifestyles at Montrose, 2430 Mary Hill Road, is a 55-plus purpose-built rental completed in 2023 by Quantum Properties, directly beside Montrose Square at 2180 Kelly Avenue — do not borrow its age label for Montrose Square.
The Port Coquitlam Community Centre at 2150 Wilson Avenue — three arenas, leisure pool, fitness centre and the Terry Fox Library — fully opened October 2, 2021, within the downtown condo shelf.
There is no hospital inside Port Coquitlam: the serving hospital is Eagle Ridge Hospital at 475 Guildford Way in Port Moody.
43 (SD43) catchments are by address, so run the condo's own address before relying on a school name.

Two manufactured-home parks that appear in Port Coquitlam searches — Hideaway Park, 4200 Dewdney Trunk Road, and Wildwood Park, 201 Cayer Street — are both in the City of Coquitlam, not Port Coquitlam.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Condos: costs and taxes

items.t: Port Coquitlam's 2026 residential municipal tax rate is 2.1985 dollars per $1,000 of assessed value, under the Annual Tax Rates Bylaw, 2026, No. 4441, with taxes due July 2, 2026.

Condo utility charges are flat annual fees, billed separately from tax: for 2026 the City lists an apartment unit at $456 for water and $458 for sewer, with utility bills due March 31, 2026 and a 5 percent penalty after that date.
Solid waste fees are billed on the annual property tax notice, and only multi-family homes that opted in to City waste collection pay them.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Condos: getting around

items.t: arriving Waterfront at 6:40 to 8:40 a.m., five eastbound afternoon returns, and no weekend or statutory holiday service, per TransLink's timetable.

There is no SkyTrain station in Port Coquitlam; TransLink's regional map shows the Millennium Line ending its eastward run through Coquitlam, with Port Coquitlam served by bus connections to Coquitlam Central Station.
Route 160 runs between Port Coquitlam Station and Kootenay Loop in Vancouver through Port Moody and Burnaby, per TransLink's route listing — the all-day bus alternative to the peak-only train.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Condos: risks and due diligence

items.t: Flood is the first check for a downtown condo: the City states a significant portion of Port Coquitlam is within the Fraser or Pitt River floodplain behind dyke infrastructure, and flood plain maps are posted at portcoquitlam.ca/flood.

Flood Construction Levels are in Schedule B of Zoning Bylaw, 2008, No. 3630 — the bylaw's own flood plans are where a buyer confirms the level that applied to a specific downtown building. - Zoning Bylaw 2008.pdf

The Cedar Drainage Pump Station upgrade, in the dike system at the northeast end of the city, was in tendering with construction set for summer 2026 to summer 2027 and completion expected late summer 2027, per the City's capital projects page.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Port Coquitlam

Port Coquitlam has a small-city feel, with a real downtown on Shaughnessy Street, a West Coast Express station and the Traboulay PoCo Trail looping around the city. Compared with Coquitlam and Port Moody, people choose PoCo for value, established neighbourhoods like Mary Hill, Citadel and Oxford Heights, and newer Riverwood townhomes.

Strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable anywhere in British Columbia since November 24, 2022, so an older Port Coquitlam bylaw package that still prints a rental cap does not bind a new owner. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw, and at Mayfair Terrace the registered 55-plus bylaw still limits who may live in the unit even when it is rented.
